# Data Codebook

Texas-calibrated pure simulation: 832 districts, seven years, no adjustment covariates.
The codebook is also available directly on the [Data page](data.html#codebook).

## Codebook

Both datasets use the same ten variables. Each contains **5,824 district-year observations**.
District and year jointly identify a row.

| Variable | Definition |
|---|---|
| `state` | State whose SEDA-derived parameters calibrate the simulation: TX. |
| `district_id` | Synthetic district identifier, 1-832. Does not identify an actual district. |
| `year` | Study year, 1-7; not a calendar year. |
| `cohort` | Adoption group: treated_year5, treated_year6, or never. The traditional dataset has no Year 6 cohort. |
| `treatment_start_year` | First treated year: 5 or 6. Zero means never treated. |
| `treated_ever` | 1 if the district receives treatment during the study; otherwise 0. |
| `treated` | 1 from adoption onward; 0 before adoption and for never-treated districts. |
| `event_time` | Year minus adoption year: -1 is the year before adoption, 0 is the first treated year. Missing for never-treated districts. |
| `outcome_std` | Continuous simulated achievement relative to the mean and SD of the full untreated Texas panel. Effects are added after standardization. |
| `outcome_raw` | Same outcome in illustrative score points: $50+10\times outcome\_std$. Not a real test scale; no fixed minimum or maximum. |

**Outcome scales:** An effect of 0.20 on outcome_std equals 2 points on outcome_raw.
The Hands-on R Lab uses outcome_raw. Observed outcomes are not restandardized after treatment.

Only event_time has missing values, for never-treated districts (NA in CSV and system missing in Stata).
There are no adjustment covariates. True effects and untreated counterfactuals are retained separately
for instructor validation.

## Generation

Seed: 20261014. Between-district variance: 0.52442729; year-effect variance: 0.22445925;
residual variance: 0.26817536; AR(1) correlation: 0.60983771.
The generator draws a baseline per district, one shared shock per year, and an independent
stationary AR(1) error path per district. It standardizes the full untreated panel, then randomly
assigns cohorts and adds effects. The two datasets share the same untreated panel.
This gives parallel untreated trends in expectation, not exactly equal sample trends.

Traditional effects are 0.20 SD in all treated periods. Staggered effects are 0.10, 0.20, and
0.30 SD for the Year 5 cohort, and 0.15 and 0.25 SD for the Year 6 cohort.
Both true Simple ATTs are 2 raw points. Seven years, workshop cohort shares, and effect schedules
are adaptations of the original pure simulation, not an exact replication of the paper's scenarios.
